# Fixtures for the WhatsApp providers

Sample payloads for `gupshup.ts`, `webhooks.ts` (messages and statuses) and `statuses.ts`. None of them came from a call to a real service: nothing in this folder has touched Gupshup or Meta.

**Copied from Gupshup's partner documentation, read on 11 Nov 2026.** Changes from the pages: customers' numbers became `919800000001` and profile names became `CUSTOMER_NAME`. The ids, timestamps, error codes and structure are as published. Where the page writes a number as a string or as a number, the fixture keeps the page's choice.

- `gupshup-v3-status-set-callback.json`, `-enqueued.json`, `-sent.json`, `-delivered.json`, `-read.json`, `-failed.json`, `-failed-internal.json`, `gupshup-v3-message-audio.json`, `gupshup-v3-message-image.json`, `gupshup-v3-message-call-permission-reply.json` come from https://partner-docs.gupshup.io/docs/events (updated 30 Oct 2026). These are the "V3" events: Meta's body plus `gs_app_id`, with `gs_id` on statuses. "Failed (internal)" is Gupshup's own refusal before Meta saw the message. It has no wamid, no metadata and no `gs_app_id`.
- `gupshup-v3-message-text.json` and `gupshup-v3-status-read-passthrough.json` come from https://partner-docs.gupshup.io/docs/whatsapp-passthrough-apis-for-partners (updated 21 Jul 2026). In that page's status example, `id` is a second UUID and not a wamid, while the events page has a wamid there. This is why the parser keeps both ids and the record is searched for either.
- `gupshup-v3-send-reply.json`, `gupshup-error-authentication.json` and `gupshup-error-callback-billing.json` come from https://partner-docs.gupshup.io/docs/whatsapp-passthrough-apis-for-partners (the reply's id) and https://partner-docs.gupshup.io/reference/post_partner-app-appid-v3-text-message (the error bodies, the same on every v3 message page).

**Copied from Meta's documentation, read on 11 Nov 2026:**

- `meta-status-failed.json` comes from https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages/status.md ("a message that failed to be sent"). Meta's delivered example is in `templates/commerce/bookings/test/fixtures/whatsapp-webhook-status-delivered.json`.

**What Gupshup's docs do not show:** a v3 callback for a tapped reply button or list row. The tests wrap Meta's own examples (`templates/commerce/bookings/test/fixtures/whatsapp-webhook-button-reply.json` and `-list-reply.json`) in Gupshup's `gs_app_id`. The call-permission reply above shows Gupshup keeping Meta's `interactive` object as Meta writes it. A real Gupshup app must confirm this (Deferred.md).

**Gupshup self-serve (item 11c), read on 12 Nov 2026 on docs.gupshup.io.** The `gupshup-selfserve-*` files. Nothing here came from a call to a real service. I fetched the raw pages with `curl https://docs.gupshup.io/<path>.md` and copied the JSON from the pages' own code blocks. Changes from the pages: customers' numbers became `919800000001` (the pages mask them like `918x98xx21x4`), names became `CUSTOMER_NAME`, media links became `example.invalid`, and the app names are the pages' own (`DemoApp`, `DemoAPI`, `docdeck`). Where a file is not the page's block, it says so below. A real Gupshup app must confirm every one (Deferred.md).

- `gupshup-selfserve-send-reply.json`: the success body, with the page's example id. https://docs.gupshup.io/docs/template-messages.md and https://docs.gupshup.io/reference/session-text-message.md (which also lists 400 "Invalid Destination" or "Invalid App Details", 401 authentication failed, 429 too many requests). `gupshup-selfserve-error-invalid-destination.json` and `-error-invalid-app.json` are those two 400 messages in the `{ status: "error", message }` shape that page gives.
- `gupshup-selfserve-templates.json`: the template list. NOT a page block: https://docs.gupshup.io/reference/get-all-templates-for-an-app.md gives only an OpenAPI schema (properties `appId`, `buttonSupported`, `category`, `id`, `elementName`, `languageCode`, `status`, `templateType`, `data` ... and top-level `status`), so this is built from that property list with our template names. The older route `GET /sm/api/v1/template/list/{appname}` (https://docs.gupshup.io/reference/getalltemplatesforanapp) shows no response at all; its reply is assumed to be the same.
- `gupshup-selfserve-message-text.json`, `-template-button.json`: the "User Sends You A Message" and "Customer Clicked On A Quick Reply Template Message Button" blocks of https://docs.gupshup.io/docs/text.md. A tapped template button arrives as an ordinary `text` message whose payload has `type: "button"`.
- `gupshup-selfserve-message-image.json`, `-audio.json`: the Image and Audio blocks of https://docs.gupshup.io/docs/media.md.
- `gupshup-selfserve-message-list-reply.json`: the list reply block of https://docs.gupshup.io/docs/interactive, as it is (postbackText "section 1 row 1 postback payload"). `-list-reply-our-id.json` is the same shape with our own row id in `postbackText` and in `id` a Gupshup-style message id; it is not a page block.
- `gupshup-selfserve-message-quick-reply.json`: the quick reply block of the same page. Its payload is `title`, `id`, `reply` only, with NO `postbackText`, and the page describes `id` as the developer-defined message id from the send request (our `msgid`), which every button of the message shares. `-quick-reply-postback.json` is the shape https://docs.gupshup.io/reference/postback-text-support.md shows for a quick-reply button that carries a postback (`payload { text, type: "button", postbackText }`), a page about template buttons. Whether a session message's quick reply carries `postbackText` is not shown by any page.
- `gupshup-selfserve-event-enqueued.json`, `-sent.json`, `-delivered.json`, `-read.json`, `-failed.json` (the "sync failed" block, code 1008), `-failed-window.json` (the "async failed" block, code 470, "more than 24 hours have passed since the customer last replied"): https://docs.gupshup.io/docs/message-events.md. `id` is Gupshup's id on enqueued and failed and WhatsApp's on sent, delivered and read, with `gsId` beside it on those.
